answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic stake burning for every validator node. Provisioning identities across isolated environments—from a temperate grove of walnut trees to a cedar outpost or a frozen tundra server cluster—imposes superlinear cost scaling: an attacker creating k nodes must burn O(k^2) tokens via non-refundable cryptographic commitments, rendering mass-identity flooding economically prohibitive.
